25: /** A {@link BreakIterator} that splits sentences using an OpenNLP sentence chunking model. */
26: public final class OpenNLPSentenceBreakIterator extends BreakIterator {
27: 
28:   private CharacterIterator text;
29:   private NLPSentenceDetectorOp sentenceOp;
30: 
31:   public OpenNLPSentenceBreakIterator(NLPSentenceDetectorOp sentenceOp) {
32:     this.sentenceOp = sentenceOp;
33:   }
34: 
35:   @Override
36:   public int current() {
37:     return text.getIndex();
38:   }
39: 
40:   @Override
41:   public int first() {
42:     sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(0);
43:     sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
44:     text.setIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
45:     return current();
46:   }
47: 
48:   @Override
49:   public int last() {
50:     int[] sentenceStarts = sentenceOp.getSentenceStarts();
51:     if (sentenceStarts.length > 0) {
52:       sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(sentenceStarts.length - 1);
53:       sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(text.getEndIndex());
54:       text.setIndex(text.getEndIndex());
55:     } else { // there are no sentences; both the first and last positions are the begin index
56:       sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(0);
57:       sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
58:       text.setIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
59:     }
60:     return current();
61:   }
62: 
63:   @Override
64:   public int next() {
65:     int[] sentenceStarts = sentenceOp.getSentenceStarts();
66:     if (text.getIndex() == text.getEndIndex() || 0 == sentenceStarts.length) {
67:       return DONE;
68:     } else if (sentenceOp.getCurrentSentence() < sentenceStarts.length - 1) {
69:       int currentSentence = sentenceOp.getCurrentSentence() + 1;
70:       sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(currentSentence);
71:       sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(sentenceStarts[currentSentence]);
72:       text.setIndex(sentenceStarts[currentSentence]);
73:       return current();
74:     } else {
75:       return last();
76:     }
77:   }
78: 
79:   @Override
80:   public int following(int pos) {
81:     int[] sentenceStarts = sentenceOp.getSentenceStarts();
82:     if (pos < text.getBeginIndex() || pos > text.getEndIndex()) {
83:       throw new IllegalArgumentException("offset out of bounds");
84:     } else if (0 == sentenceStarts.length) {
85:       text.setIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
86:       return DONE;
87:     } else if (pos >= sentenceStarts[sentenceStarts.length - 1]) {
88:       // this conflicts with the javadocs, but matches actual behavior (Oracle has a bug in
89:       // something)
90:       // https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-8015110
91:       text.setIndex(text.getEndIndex());
92:       sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(sentenceStarts.length - 1);
93:       sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(text.getEndIndex());
94:       return DONE;
95:     } else { // there are at least two sentences
96:       sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence((sentenceStarts.length - 1) / 2); // start search from the middle
97:       moveToSentenceAt(pos, 0, sentenceStarts.length - 2);
98:       int currentSentence = sentenceOp.getCurrentSentence() + 1;
99:       sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(currentSentence);
100:       sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(sentenceStarts[currentSentence]);
101:       text.setIndex(sentenceStarts[currentSentence]);
102:       return current();
103:     }
104:   }
105: 
106:   /** Binary search over sentences */
107:   private void moveToSentenceAt(int pos, int minSentence, int maxSentence) {
108:     int[] sentenceStarts = sentenceOp.getSentenceStarts();
109:     int currentSentence = sentenceOp.getCurrentSentence();
110:     int beginIndex = sentenceOp.getBeginIndex();
111:     int endIndex = sentenceOp.getEndIndex();
112:     if (text == null || pos < beginIndex) {
113:       return;
114:     }
115:     if (minSentence != maxSentence) {
116:       if (pos < sentenceStarts[currentSentence]) {
117:         int newMaxSentence = currentSentence - 1;
118:         currentSentence = minSentence + (currentSentence - minSentence) / 2;
119:         sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(currentSentence);
120:         sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(sentenceStarts[currentSentence]);
121:         moveToSentenceAt(pos, minSentence, newMaxSentence);
122:       } else if (pos >= sentenceStarts[currentSentence + 1]) {
123:         int newMinSentence = currentSentence + 1;
124:         currentSentence = maxSentence - (maxSentence - currentSentence) / 2;
125:         sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(currentSentence);
126:         sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(sentenceStarts[currentSentence]);
127:         moveToSentenceAt(pos, newMinSentence, maxSentence);
128:       }
129:     } else {
130:       assert currentSentence == minSentence;
131:       assert pos >= sentenceStarts[currentSentence];
132:       assert (currentSentence == sentenceStarts.length - 1 && pos <= endIndex)
133:           || pos < sentenceStarts[currentSentence + 1];
134:       sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(Math.min(pos, endIndex));
135:     }
136:     // we have arrived - nothing to do
137:   }
138: 
139:   @Override
140:   public int previous() {
141:     int[] sentenceStarts = sentenceOp.getSentenceStarts();
142:     if (text.getIndex() == text.getBeginIndex()) {
143:       return DONE;
144:     } else {
145:       if (0 == sentenceStarts.length) {
146:         text.setIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
147:         return DONE;
148:       }
149:       if (text.getIndex() == text.getEndIndex()) {
150:         sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(sentenceStarts[sentenceOp.getCurrentSentence()]);
151:         text.setIndex(sentenceStarts[sentenceOp.getCurrentSentence()]);
152:       } else {
153:         int currentSentence = sentenceOp.getCurrentSentence() - 1;
154:         sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(currentSentence);
155:         sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(sentenceStarts[currentSentence]);
156:         text.setIndex(sentenceStarts[currentSentence]);
157:       }
158:       return current();
159:     }
160:   }
161: 
162:   @Override
163:   public int preceding(int pos) {
164:     int[] sentenceStarts = sentenceOp.getSentenceStarts();
165:     int beginIndex = sentenceOp.getBeginIndex();
166:     int endIndex = sentenceOp.getEndIndex();
167:     if (pos < beginIndex || pos > endIndex) {
168:       throw new IllegalArgumentException("offset out of bounds");
169:     } else if (0 == sentenceStarts.length) {
170:       sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(0);
171:       sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(beginIndex);
172:       text.setIndex(sentenceOp.getCurrentIndex());
173:       return DONE;
174:     } else if (pos < sentenceStarts[0]) {
175:       // this conflicts with the javadocs, but matches actual behavior (Oracle has a bug in
176:       // something)
177:       // https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-8015110
178:       sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(0);
179:       sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(beginIndex);
180:       text.setIndex(sentenceOp.getCurrentIndex());
181:       return DONE;
182:     } else {
183:       sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(sentenceStarts.length / 2); // start search from the middle
184:       moveToSentenceAt(pos, 0, sentenceStarts.length - 1);
185:       if (0 == sentenceOp.getCurrentSentence()) {
186:         sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(beginIndex);
187:         text.setIndex(sentenceOp.getCurrentIndex());
188:         return DONE;
189:       } else {
190:         int currentSentence = sentenceOp.getCurrentSentence() - 1;
191:         sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(currentSentence);
192:         int start = sentenceStarts[currentSentence];
193:         sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(start);
194:         text.setIndex(sentenceOp.getCurrentIndex());
195:         return current();
196:       }
197:     }
198:   }
199: 
200:   @Override
201:   public int next(int n) {
202:     int[] sentenceStarts = sentenceOp.getSentenceStarts();
203:     int currentSentence = sentenceOp.getCurrentSentence() + n;
204:     sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(currentSentence);
205:     if (n < 0) {
206:       if (text.getIndex() == text.getEndIndex()) {
207:         currentSentence++;
208:         sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(currentSentence);
209:       }
210:       if (currentSentence < 0) {
211:         sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(0);
212:         sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
213:         text.setIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
214:         return DONE;
215:       } else {
216:         sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(sentenceStarts[currentSentence]);
217:         text.setIndex(sentenceStarts[currentSentence]);
218:       }
219:     } else if (n > 0) {
220:       if (currentSentence >= sentenceStarts.length) {
221:         currentSentence = sentenceStarts.length - 1;
222:         sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(currentSentence);
223:         sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(text.getEndIndex());
224:         text.setIndex(text.getEndIndex());
225:         return DONE;
226:       } else {
227:         sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(sentenceStarts[currentSentence]);
228:         text.setIndex(sentenceStarts[currentSentence]);
229:       }
230:     }
231:     return current();
232:   }
233: 
234:   @Override
235:   public CharacterIterator getText() {
236:     return text;
237:   }
238: 
239:   @Override
240:   public void setText(CharacterIterator newText) {
241:     text = newText;
242:     text.setIndex(text.getBeginIndex());
243:     Span[] spans = sentenceOp.splitSentences(sentenceOp.extractText(text));
244:     int beginIndex = text.getBeginIndex();
245:     int[] sentenceStarts = new int[spans.length];
246:     for (int i = 0; i < spans.length; ++i) {
247:       // Adjust start positions to match those of the passed-in CharacterIterator
248:       sentenceStarts[i] = spans[i].getStart() + beginIndex;
249:     }
250:     sentenceOp.setSentenceStarts(sentenceStarts);
251:     sentenceOp.setCurrentSentence(0);
252:     sentenceOp.setBeginIndex(beginIndex);
253:     sentenceOp.setEndIndex(text.getEndIndex());
254:     sentenceOp.setCurrentIndex(text.getIndex());
255:     if (sentenceStarts.length > 1) {
256:       moveToSentenceAt(beginIndex, 0, sentenceStarts.length - 1);
257:     }
258:   }

part.text: All 9 tests pass, including the regression test `testPrecedingWithTwoSentences` for this issue. The fix was a one-line change in `OpenNLPSentenceBreakIterator.preceding()` (lucene/analysis/opennlp/src/java/org/apache/lucene/analysis/opennlp/OpenNLPSentenceBreakIterator.java:183), changing the binary-search start index from `sentenceStarts.length / 2` to `(sentenceStarts.length - 1) / 2` so it never initializes past the valid `sentenceStarts` range used by `moveToSentenceAt` (which previously caused an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` when there were exactly two sentences).
